148	//  The shared-memory matrix descriptor encodes how the 128-bit core-matrix
149	//  rows are interleaved in smem to avoid bank conflicts on the wgmma read.
150	//  CRITICAL: the descriptor's layout_type field (bits 63:62) does NOT use a
151	//  size-ascending encoding. The hardware/CUTLASS encoding is
152	//  (cute/arch/mma_sm90_desc.hpp LayoutType, verified):
153	//    NONE/INTERLEAVE = 0,  SWIZZLE_128B = 1,  SWIZZLE_64B = 2,  SWIZZLE_32B = 3.
154	//  (An earlier draft had 32B=1/128B=3 swapped; the correctness path uses NONE=0
155	//  so it was unaffected, but the perf-phase swizzle modes MUST use these values.)
156	//
157	//  CORRECTNESS-PATH NOTE (deviation flagged in the report): the gated /
158	//  tested numerics path ships swizzle = NONE (kSwizzleNone). NONE is a
159	//  fully-legal descriptor mode (§<ip>.4) and is the layout the
160	//  correctness gates validate against torch. The 128B-swizzle layout is a
161	//  PERF-PHASE optimization (bank-conflict elimination on the smem read) and
162	//  is exposed here as the template parameter the model headers will select
163	//  once the quiet-GPU perf phase measures it; it is NOT required for any
164	//  correctness gate. See DESIGN §4.1 ("specify the 128-byte-swizzle layout"
165	//  is the perf target; phase-1 staging uses cp.async, §4.1 item 3).
166	// =========================================================================
167	enum SwizzleMode : uint32_t {
168	    kSwizzleNone = 0,   // INTERLEAVE / no swizzle (the correctness-path layout)
169	    kSwizzle128B = 1,   // SWIZZLE_128B
170	    kSwizzle64B  = 2,   // SWIZZLE_64B
171	    kSwizzle32B  = 3,   // SWIZZLE_32B

174	// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
175	//  generic-smem-pointer → matrix-descriptor start address.
176	//  PTX ISA §<ip>.4: the descriptor's bits 13-0 hold the start address of
177	//  the matrix in shared memory, encoded as the 18-bit smem byte address with
178	//  the low 4 bits dropped — i.e. addr_field = (smem_byte_addr & 0x3FFFF) >> 4.
179	//  The low 4 bits MUST be zero (16-byte alignment) or they are silently lost.
180	// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
181	__device__ __forceinline__ uint32_t smem_desc_encode_addr(const void* smem_ptr) {
182	#if defined(__CUDA_ARCH__) && (__CUDA_ARCH__ >= 900)
183	    uint32_t a = static_cast<uint32_t>(__cvta_generic_to_shared(smem_ptr));
184	    return (a & 0x3FFFFu) >> 4;
185	#else
186	    (void)smem_ptr;
187	    return 0u;
188	#endif
189	}

191	// =========================================================================
192	//  Shared-memory matrix descriptor (PTX ISA §<ip>.4).
193	//
194	//  64-bit layout (bit ranges per the ISA table):
195	//    bits  13: 0  start address (smem byte addr >> 4)
196	//    bits  15:14  (reserved / 0)
197	//    bits  29:16  leading-dimension byte offset (LBO) >> 4
198	//    bits  31:30  (reserved / 0)
199	//    bits  45:32  stride-dimension byte offset (SBO) >> 4
200	//    bits  48:46  (reserved / 0)
201	//    bits  51:49  matrix base offset (for swizzle; 0 for our tiles)
202	//    bits  61:52  (reserved / 0)
203	//    bits  63:62  swizzle / layout mode (0 none / 1 128B / 2 64B / 3 32B —
204	//                 the CUTLASS LayoutType encoding, see SwizzleMode above)
205	//
206	//  LBO and SBO are the byte offsets between consecutive "core matrices" along
207	//  the leading and stride dimensions respectively (§<ip>.3 "Strides").
208	//  Both are encoded >>4 (16-byte granular). The exact (LBO,SBO) depend on the
209	//  operand's smem tile layout; the make_desc_*_kmajor builders below compute
210	//  them for the canonical row-major-K bf16 tiles the model headers stage.
211	// =========================================================================
212	struct SmemDesc {
213	    uint64_t desc;
214	};
215	
216	// Low-level builder: caller supplies LBO/SBO in BYTES; we apply the >>4 and
217	// the swizzle field. Use the make_desc_*_kmajor convenience wrappers unless
218	// you have a bespoke smem layout.
219	template <SwizzleMode Swizzle = kSwizzleNone>
220	__device__ __forceinline__ SmemDesc make_smem_desc(
221	    const void* smem_base, uint32_t lbo_bytes, uint32_t sbo_bytes,
222	    uint32_t base_offset = 0u
223	) {
224	    SmemDesc d;
225	#if defined(__CUDA_ARCH__) && (__CUDA_ARCH__ >= 900)
226	    uint64_t addr = static_cast<uint64_t>(smem_desc_encode_addr(smem_base));
227	    uint64_t lbo  = static_cast<uint64_t>((lbo_bytes >> 4) & 0x3FFFu);
228	    uint64_t sbo  = static_cast<uint64_t>((sbo_bytes >> 4) & 0x3FFFu);
229	    uint64_t bo   = static_cast<uint64_t>(base_offset & 0x7u);
230	    uint64_t sw   = static_cast<uint64_t>(Swizzle & 0x3u);
231	    d.desc = (addr)                 // bits 13:0
232	           | (lbo << 16)            // bits 29:16
233	           | (sbo << 32)            // bits 45:32
234	           | (bo  << 49)            // bits 51:49
235	           | (sw  << 62);           // bits 63:62
236	#else
237	    (void)smem_base; (void)lbo_bytes; (void)sbo_bytes; (void)base_offset;
238	    d.desc = 0;
239	#endif
240	    return d;
241	}

256	//  row-major block of 128-bit rows: core-matrix 0 (k 0..7) occupies the first
257	//  MN*8 bf16 (MN*16 bytes), core-matrix 1 (k 8..15) the next MN*16 bytes.

291	//  fp32 accumulator fragment for an m64×N output tile.
292	//  PTX ISA §<ip>.3 "Register fragment for .f32 accumulators" (the
293	//  m64nNk16 wgmma writes its output across the 128 warpgroup threads).
294	//
295	//  Fragment layout (the ISA figure, decoded):
296	//    - 128 threads = 4 warps; the M=64 rows are split so that
297	//        warp w  (w in 0..3)  owns rows  [16*w .. 16*w+15],
298	//      and within a warp, lane L owns two row-groups:
299	//        row_hi = 16*w + (L/4)        (rows 0..7 of the warp's block)
300	//        row_lo = row_hi + 8          (rows 8..15)
301	//    - The N columns are held as N/2 fp32 registers per thread, in pairs:
302	//        register pair (2c, 2c+1) holds columns (col_base+0, col_base+1)
303	//        where col_base = (L%4)*2 + 8*(c/2_grouped)...  [the (col%8) + 8*(c>>1)
304	//      grouping of the ISA]. We expose the exact decode via frag_row()/
305	//      frag_col() so the epilogue (and the self-test) maps register i of
306	//      lane L (in warp w) to the (row,col) of the 64×N output it represents.
307	//
308	//  We store N/2 floats. c[2*g + p] is the p-th (p in {0,1}) of register-group
309	//  g (g in [0, N/4) for the "even/odd column pair" grouping). The helpers
310	//  frag_row(lane,i) / frag_col(lane,i) give the global (row,col) so a single
311	//  authoritative decode is shared by the epilogue store AND the gate's
312	//  reference comparison (no chance of a mismatched private decode).
313	// =========================================================================
314	template <int N>
315	struct WgmmaAccum {
316	    static_assert(N % 8 == 0, "wgmma N must be a multiple of 8");
317	    static constexpr int kRegs = N / 2;   // fp32 regs per thread
318	    float c[kRegs];
319	
320	    __device__ __forceinline__ void zero() {
321	        #pragma unroll
322	        for (int i = 0; i < kRegs; ++i) c[i] = 0.0f;
323	    }
324	};

326	// --- Authoritative fragment decode (PTX ISA §<ip>.3, .f32 accumulators) -
327	// For thread `tid_in_wg` in [0,128) and register index `i` in [0, N/2):
328	//   warp = tid_in_wg / 32 ; lane = tid_in_wg % 32.
329	//   The 64 M-rows are partitioned warp-major: rows [16*warp, 16*warp+16).
330	//   lane bits decode within the warp's 16-row × N block as in the ISA figure:
331	//     group g = i / 2 ; sub p = i % 2.
332	//     row = 16*warp + (lane / 4) + 8 * (g % 2 == 0 ? 0 : 0)   -- see below.
333	//
334	// The ISA C-fragment for .m64nNk16.f32 lays out each lane's N/2 elements as
335	// (over the row pair r0=lane/4, r1=r0+8) interleaved column pairs. The precise
336	// closed form, validated by the A=I gate, is:
337	//   group_of_8 = i / 8 ;   within = i % 8
338	//   row = 16*warp + (lane/4) + 8*(within / 4)
339	//   col = (lane%4)*2 + (within % 2) + 8*group_of_8 + ...
340	// To keep ONE source of truth that the gate verifies bit-for-bit, the decode
341	// is implemented below in the exact factored form the ISA figure gives for
342	// the 16x8 sub-blocks the f32 accumulator tiles across N.
343	__device__ __forceinline__ void wgmma_frag_decode(
344	    int tid_in_wg, int i, int N, int& row, int& col
345	) {
346	    const int warp = tid_in_wg >> 5;       // 0..3
347	    const int lane = tid_in_wg & 31;       // 0..31
348	    // Each 16x8 output sub-block (one "n8" column slab) contributes 4 regs
349	    // per thread (8 rows split into 2 row-halves × ... ). The ISA's .f32
350	    // fragment for an n8 slab gives, per lane:
351	    //   reg 0 -> (row = lane/4,       col = (lane%4)*2 + 0)
352	    //   reg 1 -> (row = lane/4,       col = (lane%4)*2 + 1)
353	    //   reg 2 -> (row = lane/4 + 8,   col = (lane%4)*2 + 0)
354	    //   reg 3 -> (row = lane/4 + 8,   col = (lane%4)*2 + 1)
355	    // and successive n8 slabs add 8 to the column. With N columns there are
356	    // N/8 slabs × 4 regs = N/2 regs (matches kRegs).
357	    const int slab   = i >> 2;             // which n8 column slab (0..N/8-1)
358	    const int within = i & 3;              // 0..3 within the slab
359	    const int row_half = within >> 1;      // 0 -> rows 0..7, 1 -> rows 8..15
360	    const int col_par  = within & 1;       // 0 or 1 column within the pair
361	    row = 16 * warp + (lane >> 2) + 8 * row_half;
362	    col = (lane & 3) * 2 + col_par + 8 * slab;
363	    (void)N;
364	}

111	    static constexpr uint32_t kARowStride = kWgmmaAtomK * (uint32_t)sizeof(__nv_bfloat16); // 32
112	    static constexpr uint32_t kBRowStride = kWgmmaAtomK * (uint32_t)sizeof(__nv_bfloat16); // 32
113	    // tx-bytes for the stage's two cp.async transactions (full barrier expects).
114	    static constexpr int kStageTxBytes = kStageBytes;
115	};
116	
117	// =========================================================================
118	//  TilePipeline — the Depth-stage ring + its mbarriers.
119	//
120	//  smem layout the caller hands us (one contiguous arena, 16B-aligned):
121	//    [ stage0 A | stage0 B | stage1 A | stage1 B | ... | full[Depth] | empty[Depth] ]
122	//  where each stage's A is 16B-aligned (kAElems is a multiple of 8 bf16 = 16B)
123	//  and B follows (also 16B-multiple for the design's N). The two mbarrier
124	//  arrays are 8-byte words.
125	//
126	//  Two barriers per stage (the canonical producer/consumer ring):
127	//    full[s]  : producer arrives (expect_tx) when it has issued the loads for
128	//               stage s; consumer waits on it before issuing wgmma.
129	//    empty[s] : consumer arrives when it has finished consuming stage s;
130	//               producer waits on it before overwriting stage s (so the
131	//               in-flight wgmma is not clobbered). For Depth-buffering the
132	//               producer can run Depth stages ahead before it must wait.
133	//
134	//  Phase parity: each barrier flips parity every time its expected arrivals
135	//  complete. We track per-stage parity bits for full and empty.
136	// =========================================================================
137	//  NOTE on storage: Mbarrier (warp_specialize.cuh) is a thin wrapper around a
138	//  single smem word and has only an `explicit Mbarrier(ull*)` constructor (no
139	//  default ctor). To avoid needing a default-constructible barrier array, we
140	//  store ONLY the barrier-word base pointer and construct an Mbarrier
141	//  on-demand via full(s) / empty(s) — a zero-cost wrapper around the word.
142	template <int N, int Depth>
143	struct TilePipeline {
144	    __nv_bfloat16* ring;          // [Depth] × (A|B) tiles, 16B-aligned
145	    unsigned long long* bars;     // [2*Depth] mbarrier words: full[Depth] then empty[Depth]
146	
147	    // Construct over a caller-provided smem arena. `arena` points at the start
148	    // of the ring (must be 16B-aligned). The barrier words follow the tiles.
149	    __device__ __forceinline__ TilePipeline(void* arena)
150	        : ring(reinterpret_cast<__nv_bfloat16*>(arena)),
151	          bars(reinterpret_cast<unsigned long long*>(
152	              reinterpret_cast<char*>(arena) +
153	              (size_t)Depth * TileGeom<N>::kStageBytes)) {}
154	
155	    __device__ __forceinline__ Mbarrier full(int s)  { return Mbarrier(bars + s); }
156	    __device__ __forceinline__ Mbarrier empty(int s) { return Mbarrier(bars + Depth + s); }
157	
158	    __device__ __forceinline__ __nv_bfloat16* stageA(int s) {
159	        return ring + (size_t)s * (TileGeom<N>::kAElems + TileGeom<N>::kBElems);
160	    }
161	    __device__ __forceinline__ __nv_bfloat16* stageB(int s) {
162	        return stageA(s) + TileGeom<N>::kAElems;
163	    }
164	
165	    // Bytes the caller must allocate as dynamic smem for this pipeline.
166	    static constexpr size_t smem_bytes() {
167	        return (size_t)Depth * TileGeom<N>::kStageBytes +
168	               (size_t)2 * Depth * sizeof(unsigned long long);
169	    }
170	
171	    // Init the barriers (one thread of the block). Each barrier expects a FULL
172	    // WARPGROUP (128) of arrivals per phase: full[] is arrived by all 128
173	    // producer threads (so the phase-flip happens-after every thread's
174	    // cp.async + wait_group, giving the consumer a warpgroup-wide visibility
175	    // guarantee), empty[] by all 128 consumer threads. (An earlier draft used
176	    // init(1) + a per-warp elect_one_sync arrive — but elect.sync elects one
177	    // leader PER WARP, so 4 warps produced 4 arrivals on a count-1 barrier,
178	    // flipping the phase an even number of times and DEADLOCKING the consumer's
179	    // try_wait.parity. count=128 + all-threads-arrive is the correct contract.)
180	    __device__ __forceinline__ void init_barriers() {
181	        if (threadIdx.x == 0) {
182	            #pragma unroll
183	            for (int s = 0; s < Depth; ++s) {
184	                full(s).init(128);
185	                empty(s).init(128);
186	            }
187	        }
188	    }
189	};
190	
191	// =========================================================================
192	//  Producer-side staging of ONE K-tile (stage `slot`, k-index `k`) via
193	//  cp.async (DESIGN §4.2 WG0). Issues 16-byte cp.async copies of the A and B
194	//  tiles from HBM into the ring slot, then the elected leader does
195	//  arrive_expect_tx(tx) on the stage's `full` barrier so the consumer knows
196	//  the bytes are inbound. cp.async + mbarrier transaction-count is the
197	//  standard Hopper async-load handshake.
198	//
199	//  NOTE: this uses cp.async (.cg.16), NOT TMA — DESIGN §4.1 item 3 makes TMA
200	//  explicitly phase-2; phase-1 staging is cp.async (already overlaps load
201	//  latency). For cp.async the transaction completion is signalled via
202	//  cp.async.mbarrier.arrive (the bytes are counted by the barrier). We model
203	//  that with arrive_expect_tx on the producer leader + cp_async_commit, and
204	//  the consumer's try_wait/parity gates on it.
205	// =========================================================================
206	template <int N, int Depth>
207	__device__ __forceinline__ void pipeline_produce_ktile(
208	    TilePipeline<N, Depth>& pipe, int slot, int k,
209	    const __nv_bfloat16* gA, const __nv_bfloat16* gB, int /*k_steps*/
210	) {
211	#if defined(__CUDA_ARCH__) && (__CUDA_ARCH__ >= 900)
212	    const int wtid = threadIdx.x & 127;          // 0..127 within WG0
213	    __nv_bfloat16* dA = pipe.stageA(slot);
214	    __nv_bfloat16* dB = pipe.stageB(slot);
215	    const __nv_bfloat16* sA = gA + (size_t)k * TileGeom<N>::kAElems;  // row-major MxK
216	    const __nv_bfloat16* sB = gB + (size_t)k * TileGeom<N>::kBElems;  // row-major NxK
217	
218	    // 16B (8 bf16) cp.async copies SCATTERED into the canonical Major-K layout
219	    // (two stacked 8-wide core matrices) make_desc_*_kmajor requires. A global
220	    // row (mn, 0..15) splits into two 16B halves: half 0 (k 0..7) lands at
221	    // mn*8, half 1 (k 8..15) at MN*8 + mn*8 — both 16B-aligned. kVec=8 bf16.
222	    constexpr int kVec = 16 / (int)sizeof(__nv_bfloat16);   // 8 bf16 / 16B
223	    // A: MN=64. 64 rows × 2 halves = 128 vectors.
224	    constexpr int kAHalves = 64 * (kWgmmaAtomK / kVec);     // 64*2 = 128
225	    for (int v = wtid; v < kAHalves; v += 128) {
226	        const int mn = v >> 1;                  // 0..63
227	        const int half = v & 1;                 // 0 or 1
228	        const __nv_bfloat16* src = sA + (size_t)mn * kWgmmaAtomK + (size_t)half * kVec;
229	        __nv_bfloat16* dst = dA + (size_t)half * (64 * kVec) + (size_t)mn * kVec;
230	        prim::cp_async_cg_16(dst, src);
231	    }
232	    // B: MN=N. N rows × 2 halves vectors.
233	    constexpr int kBHalves = N * (kWgmmaAtomK / kVec);      // N*2
234	    for (int v = wtid; v < kBHalves; v += 128) {
235	        const int mn = v >> 1;                  // 0..N-1
236	        const int half = v & 1;
237	        const __nv_bfloat16* src = sB + (size_t)mn * kWgmmaAtomK + (size_t)half * kVec;
238	        __nv_bfloat16* dst = dB + (size_t)half * (N * kVec) + (size_t)mn * kVec;
239	        prim::cp_async_cg_16(dst, src);
240	    }
241	    prim::cp_async_commit();
242	    // Drain THIS stage's group before signalling full, so the consumer's wgmma
243	    // (which reads smem directly, not through the mbarrier transaction count)
244	    // sees landed bytes. cp.async.wait_group<0> + the arrive gives a correct
245	    // handshake without relying on cp.async.mbarrier.arrive byte-counting
246	    // (which would require the .mbarrier.arrive variant; we keep the portable
247	    // wait_group form from primitives.cuh and use the mbarrier purely as the
248	    // cross-warpgroup ready signal). DESIGN §4.2: one async-proxy fence per
249	    // hand-off.
250	    prim::cp_async_wait_group<0>();
251	    fence_async_proxy();
252	    // ALL 128 producer threads arrive (barrier count=128). Each thread's
253	    // arrive happens-after its own cp.async + wait_group<0>, so the phase-flip
254	    // (on the 128th arrive) is visibility-ordered after every staged byte.
255	    pipe.full(slot).arrive();       // signal: stage `slot` is ready to consume
256	#else
257	    (void)pipe; (void)slot; (void)k; (void)gA; (void)gB;
258	#endif
259	}
260	
261	// =========================================================================
262	//  tc_pipelined_gemm_m64nNk16 — the turnkey single-CTA pipelined GEMM.
263	//  blockDim.x = 256: WG0 = producer (tid 0..127), WG1 = consumer (128..255).
264	//  DESIGN §4.2 producer/consumer structure, §4.3 occupancy budget.
265	//
266	//  Determinism: the consumer issues wgmma in ASCENDING k (fixed order); the
267	//  pipeline only changes operand-availability timing, not the reduction order,
268	//  so the fp32 accumulation is bit-identical to the unpipelined kchain
269	//  (DESIGN gate c).
270	// =========================================================================
271	template <int N, int Depth>
272	__device__ __forceinline__ void tc_pipelined_gemm_m64nNk16(
273	    const __nv_bfloat16* __restrict__ gA,
274	    const __nv_bfloat16* __restrict__ gB,
275	    float* __restrict__ gD, int k_steps
276	) {
277	#if defined(__CUDA_ARCH__) && (__CUDA_ARCH__ >= 900)
278	    extern __shared__ char smem_raw[];
279	    // 16B-align the ring arena.
280	    uintptr_t base = reinterpret_cast<uintptr_t>(smem_raw);
281	    uintptr_t aligned = (base + 15u) & ~uintptr_t(15u);
282	    TilePipeline<N, Depth> pipe(reinterpret_cast<void*>(aligned));
283	    pipe.init_barriers();
284	    __syncthreads();
285	
286	    const int warpgroup = threadIdx.x / 128;    // 0 = producer, 1 = consumer
287	    const bool is_producer = (warpgroup == 0);
288	
289	    // Register rebalance (DESIGN §4.2): producer few regs, consumer many.
290	    // Guarded by SG_TUNED_*_REGS != 0 (0 disables for portability/debug).
291	#if (SG_TUNED_PROD_REGS != 0) && (SG_TUNED_CONS_REGS != 0)
292	    if (is_producer) warpgroup_reg_dealloc<SG_TUNED_PROD_REGS>();
293	    else             warpgroup_reg_alloc  <SG_TUNED_CONS_REGS>();
294	#endif
295	
296	    if (is_producer) {
297	        // Producer: stage every K-tile in ascending k. With Depth buffering it
298	        // may run up to Depth stages ahead; we gate reuse of a slot on the
299	        // consumer having released it (empty[slot]).
300	        unsigned empty_parity[Depth];
301	        #pragma unroll
302	        for (int s = 0; s < Depth; ++s) empty_parity[s] = 0u;
303	        for (int k = 0; k < k_steps; ++k) {
304	            const int slot = k % Depth;
305	            // For k >= Depth, the slot was used by k-Depth; wait until the
306	            // consumer released it (empty barrier) before overwriting.
307	            if (k >= Depth) {
308	                pipe.empty(slot).wait(empty_parity[slot]);
309	                empty_parity[slot] ^= 1u;
310	            }
311	            pipeline_produce_ktile<N, Depth>(pipe, slot, k, gA, gB, k_steps);
312	        }
313	    } else {
314	        // Consumer: wgmma over each staged K-tile in ascending k. The fp32
315	        // fragment accumulates across the whole chain (first k overwrites).
316	        WgmmaAccum<N> acc;
317	        unsigned full_parity[Depth];
318	        #pragma unroll
319	        for (int s = 0; s < Depth; ++s) full_parity[s] = 0u;
320	
321	        // We can't use the kchain helper directly (it expects all descriptors
322	        // available); instead we inline the SAME choreography: one fence, then
323	        // k=0 overwrite / k>0 accumulate, commit+wait at the end. Issuing each
324	        // wgmma right after its stage is ready overlaps load and compute.
325	        wgmma_fence();
326	        for (int k = 0; k < k_steps; ++k) {
327	            const int slot = k % Depth;
328	            pipe.full(slot).wait(full_parity[slot]);
329	            full_parity[slot] ^= 1u;
330	
331	            __nv_bfloat16* aTile = pipe.stageA(slot);
332	            __nv_bfloat16* bTile = pipe.stageB(slot);
333	            SmemDesc dA = make_desc_A_kmajor</*M=*/64, kSwizzleNone>(aTile);
334	            SmemDesc dB = make_desc_B_kmajor</*N=*/N,  kSwizzleNone>(bTile);
335	            // Both operands Major-K ⇒ TransA=0, TransB=0 (cute Major::K == 0).
336	            if (k == 0) {
337	                wgmma_m64nNk16_bf16<N, /*ScaleD=*/0, /*TransA=*/0, /*TransB=*/0>(acc, dA, dB);
338	            } else {
339	                wgmma_m64nNk16_bf16<N, /*ScaleD=*/1, /*TransA=*/0, /*TransB=*/0>(acc, dA, dB);
340	            }
341	            // Commit + wait THIS issue before releasing the slot, so the
342	            // producer does not overwrite operands the async wgmma still reads.
343	            wgmma_commit_group();
344	            wgmma_wait_group<0>();
345	            // Release the slot back to the producer. ALL 128 consumer threads
346	            // arrive (barrier count=128) — see init_barriers: the per-warp elect
347	            // would give 4 arrivals on a count-1 barrier and deadlock.
348	            pipe.empty(slot).arrive();
349	        }
350	
351	        // Epilogue: store the fp32 fragment. The consumer warpgroup owns the
352	        // output; decode relative to its 128-thread group (tid-128).
353	        const int tid_in_wg = threadIdx.x - 128;
354	        #pragma unroll
355	        for (int i = 0; i < WgmmaAccum<N>::kRegs; ++i) {
356	            int row, col;
357	            wgmma_frag_decode(tid_in_wg, i, N, row, col);
358	            gD[row * N + col] = acc.c[i];
359	        }
360	    }
361	#else
362	    (void)gA; (void)gB; (void)gD; (void)k_steps;
363	#endif
364	}
365	
366	}}} // namespace sg::sm90::wgs

3	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
4	// Stage 6 — sm_90 L3 persistent-megakernel internals (§1.1–§1.4, §1.13, §1.14).
5	//
6	// This header is the **uniform scheduler + barrier substrate** that every
7	// generated L3 megakernel (csrc/fused/sm_90/*.cu) composes on top of the §3.4
8	// warp-specialization primitives (csrc/backends/cuda/sm_90/warp_specialize.cuh).
9	// It defines ONLY the cross-CTA coordination machinery; the per-(model,
10	// optimizer) compute stages live in the generated TUs.
11	//
12	// The four pieces, all sm_90-real (compile-verified via
13	// scripts/compile_to_object.sh) and degrading to a correct fallback on older
14	// arches so the codegen matrix still builds:
15	//
16	//   §1.1  TaskQueue        — a single global atomic work counter that every
17	//                            persistent CTA pulls parameter-tensor indices
18	//                            from (the ThunderKittens-interpreter pattern).
19	//   §1.2  work-stealing     — there is NO static partition: an idle CTA simply
20	//                            keeps calling TaskQueue::next(), so a CTA that
21	//                            finishes its tensor early steals the next one.
22	//                            (atomicAdd on the shared counter IS the steal.)
23	//   §1.3  sm_id()           — reads %smid so the host can pin one persistent
24	//                            CTA per SM and keep that SM's optimizer-state
25	//                            slice L2-warm across the step.
26	//   §1.4  GridBarrier       — a hand-built arrive/wait grid barrier from two
27	//                            global atomics + a sense-reversing generation
28	//                            counter. Reusable, needs NO cooperative launch
29	//                            (so it scales past the cooperative-grid CTA cap).
30	//
31	// §1.14 fences: acquire/release are placed EXPLICITLY and MINIMALLY — exactly
32	// one __threadfence() before the arrival publish and one acquire load after
33	// the release wait at the barrier, and one fence at the task hand-off. No loose
34	// fences (a loose fence here is both a correctness and a >10% perf footgun).
35	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
36	
37	#include "csrc/common/platform.h"
38	#include "csrc/backends/cuda/sm_90/warp_specialize.cuh"
39	#include <cuda_runtime.h>
40	
41	// SG_TUNED_MEGA_BLOCK — threads per persistent megakernel CTA, shared by EVERY
42	// L3 megakernel that composes this substrate (the fused elementwise megakernel
43	// + the decoder / vit / mamba model drivers + the SuperGrok2 stage). Default
44	// 256 (= two 128-thread Hopper warp-groups → byte-identical untuned build).
45	// NEEDS-PARITY before shipping a non-default winner: the §3.4 producer/consumer
46	// warp-specialization and the per-model shared staging/reduction buffers assume
47	// the 256-thread (2 warp-group) shape, so any swept value must remain a
48	// multiple of the warp-group size AND be re-validated on the H100 parity gate —
49	// the autotuner cannot prove launch-shape correctness on its own.
50	#ifndef SG_TUNED_MEGA_BLOCK
51	#define SG_TUNED_MEGA_BLOCK 256
52	#endif
53	
54	namespace sg { namespace fused {
55	
56	// =========================================================================
57	//  §1.3  SM-pinning: read the streaming-multiprocessor id via %smid.
58	//
59	//  The host launches exactly gridDim.x == #SMs CTAs (one persistent CTA per
60	//  SM) and uses sm_id() inside the kernel to index that SM's resident slice
61	//  of optimizer state, so the slice stays warm in this SM's L2 partition for
62	//  the whole step. On pre-sm_90 the asm is still valid (%smid exists since
63	//  sm_20); the guard only exists to keep a host-compile of this header clean.
64	// =========================================================================
65	__device__ __forceinline__ unsigned sm_id() {
66	#if defined(__CUDA_ARCH__)
67	    unsigned id;
68	    asm volatile("mov.u32 %0, %%smid;" : "=r"(id));
69	    return id;
70	#else
71	    return 0u;
72	#endif
73	}
74	
75	// =========================================================================
76	//  §1.1 / §1.2  TaskQueue — global work counter + work-stealing.
77	//
78	//  One int in global memory (`g_next_task`, zero-initialized by the host).
79	//  Every CTA runs:
80	//      for (int t = q.next(); t < n_tasks; t = q.next()) process(t);
81	//  next() does `atomicAdd(g_next_task, 1)` — a CTA that drains its tensor
82	//  early just grabs the next index, so faster SMs steal work from the queue
83	//  with no static load-balancing (§1.2). The atomic is the ONLY synchronizer;
84	//  task bodies are independent (one parameter tensor each), so no fence is
85	//  needed on the *pull* — the fence belongs at the grid barrier between the
86	//  forward / backward / optimizer phases (§1.4), not on the per-task pull.
87	//
88	//  By convention ONE thread per CTA (the elected leader) pulls a task and
89	//  broadcasts it to the block via shared memory; `next_block()` packages that.
90	// =========================================================================
91	struct TaskQueue {
92	    int* g_next_task;   // global counter (host memset to 0 before launch)
93	    int  n_tasks;       // total parameter tensors to process this phase
94	
95	    __device__ __forceinline__ explicit TaskQueue(int* counter, int total)
96	        : g_next_task(counter), n_tasks(total) {}
97	
98	    // Per-thread atomic pull (used when every thread independently claims work,
99	    // e.g. a warp-granular schedule). Returns a task index that may be >=
100	    // n_tasks (caller bounds-checks).
101	    __device__ __forceinline__ int next() {
102	        return atomicAdd(g_next_task, 1);
103	    }
104	
105	    // Per-CTA pull: the leader thread does the single atomicAdd and broadcasts
106	    // the claimed index to the whole block through `smem_slot`. All threads in
107	    // the block then cooperate on that one tensor. Returns the claimed index.
108	    __device__ __forceinline__ int next_block(int* smem_slot) {
109	        if (threadIdx.x == 0) {
110	            *smem_slot = atomicAdd(g_next_task, 1);
111	        }
112	        __syncthreads();
113	        int t = *smem_slot;
114	        __syncthreads();   // ensure every thread read before slot is reused
115	        return t;
116	    }
117	};
118	
119	// =========================================================================
120	//  §1.4  GridBarrier — hand-built, reusable, sense-reversing grid barrier.
121	//
122	//  State (all in global memory, host-zero-initialized):
123	//    arrived    — count of CTAs that have reached the current barrier
124	//    generation — flips/advances each time the barrier is crossed (the "sense"
125	//                 a late CTA waits on so an early CTA can't lap it)
126	//
127	//  The classic correctness hazard with a counter barrier is *reuse*: if you
128	//  just reset `arrived` to 0, a fast CTA can enter the NEXT barrier and
129	//  increment the counter before a slow CTA has observed the release of the
130	//  PREVIOUS one. The sense-reversing generation fixes this: each CTA samples
131	//  the generation on entry, then waits until the generation has ADVANCED
132	//  (the last arriver advances it), never touching `arrived` for reset on the
133	//  consumer side. The last CTA to arrive resets `arrived` to 0 and bumps the
134	//  generation in one release; everyone else spins on the generation.
135	//
136	//  Fences (§1.14):
137	//    * The releasing writes a CTA makes BEFORE the barrier (its phase output)
138	//      must be visible to peers AFTER the barrier. We publish arrival with a
139	//      __threadfence() (device-scope release) before the atomicAdd, and the
140	//      waiters do an acquire by reading the generation with volatile semantics
141	//      and a __threadfence() after the wait completes. Exactly two fences per
142	//      CTA per barrier — the minimum for a correct release/acquire pair.
143	//
144	//  Only thread 0 of each CTA participates in the cross-CTA handshake; the rest
145	//  of the block is gated by a __syncthreads() so the whole CTA leaves together.
146	// =========================================================================
147	struct GridBarrier {
148	    unsigned* g_arrived;      // CTAs arrived at current phase
149	    unsigned* g_generation;   // sense-reversing generation counter
150	    unsigned  n_ctas;         // gridDim.x (CTAs that must arrive)
151	
152	    __device__ __forceinline__ GridBarrier(unsigned* arrived,
153	                                            unsigned* generation,
154	                                            unsigned grid_ctas)
155	        : g_arrived(arrived), g_generation(generation), n_ctas(grid_ctas) {}
156	
157	    __device__ __forceinline__ void sync() const {
158	        // The block must fully reach the barrier before its leader publishes.
159	        __syncthreads();
160	
161	        if (threadIdx.x == 0) {
162	            // Sample the sense we are waiting to leave.
163	            unsigned my_gen =
164	                *reinterpret_cast<volatile unsigned*>(g_generation);
165	
166	            // §1.14 RELEASE: make this CTA's phase writes visible device-wide
167	            // BEFORE we announce arrival, so a peer that observes our arrival
168	            // (and crosses) also observes our outputs.
169	            __threadfence();
170	
171	            // Atomically join the arrival count. The CTA whose add completes
172	            // the set (== n_ctas) is the "last arriver".
173	            unsigned prev = atomicAdd(g_arrived, 1u);
174	            if (prev + 1u == n_ctas) {
175	                // Last arriver: clear the count for the NEXT phase, then bump
176	                // the generation. Order matters — reset arrived to 0 first,
177	                // then a release-store of the advanced generation so a CTA that
178	                // sees the new generation also sees arrived==0 when it next
179	                // enters. atomicExch gives the store device-scope visibility.
180	                atomicExch(g_arrived, 0u);
181	                __threadfence();
182	                atomicAdd(g_generation, 1u);
183	            } else {
184	                // Not last: spin until the generation advances past our sample.
185	                // §1.14b BACKOFF: a tight volatile-read spin hammers the L2 /
186	                // memory subsystem with the generation poll and steals issue
187	                // slots from arriving CTAs. __nanosleep parks the spinning warp
188	                // for an exponentially-growing nap (capped) so the poll rate
189	                // drops and the memory subsystem is left to the laggard CTAs.
190	                // Behavior-preserving: still exits the instant the generation
191	                // advances; only the *poll cadence* changes (sm_70+; on older
192	                // arches the asm is a no-op fallback).
193	                unsigned backoff = 32u;
194	                while (*reinterpret_cast<volatile unsigned*>(g_generation)
195	                       == my_gen) {
196	#if defined(__CUDA_ARCH__) && (__CUDA_ARCH__ >= 700)
197	                    __nanosleep(backoff);
198	                    backoff = (backoff < 1024u) ? (backoff << 1) : 1024u;
199	#endif
200	                }
201	            }
202	
203	            // §1.14 ACQUIRE: after observing the generation advance, fence so
204	            // the peers' phase writes (released above) are visible to us.
205	            __threadfence();
206	        }
207	
208	        // Release the rest of the block once the leader has crossed.
209	        __syncthreads();
210	    }
211	
212	    // #4 — barrier with a FUSED task-counter reset. The L3 phase loop used to do
213	    //   fwd → sync → reset_counter → sync → bwd → sync → reset_counter → sync
214	    // (4 grid barriers + 2 standalone in-kernel counter resets). The reset is
215	    // folded into THIS barrier's last-arriver critical section: the last CTA
216	    // zeroes `*reset_counter` BEFORE the release-store that advances the
217	    // generation, so any CTA that later observes the new generation (and thus
218	    // crosses) is guaranteed to see the counter == 0 for the next phase. That
219	    // removes the two standalone resets AND their two barriers — 4 → 2 grid
220	    // barriers per L3 step — with identical phase ordering/visibility. Pass the
221	    // task-queue counter (ctx.g_next_task) as `reset_counter`.
222	    __device__ __forceinline__ void sync_reset(int* reset_counter) const {
223	        __syncthreads();
224	
225	        if (threadIdx.x == 0) {
226	            unsigned my_gen =
227	                *reinterpret_cast<volatile unsigned*>(g_generation);
228	            __threadfence();   // §1.14 RELEASE: publish phase writes before arrival.
229	            unsigned prev = atomicAdd(g_arrived, 1u);
230	            if (prev + 1u == n_ctas) {
231	                // Last arriver: clear arrival count AND reset the task counter
232	                // for the next phase, then a release-store of the advanced
233	                // generation. Ordering: both resets, then __threadfence(), then
234	                // the generation bump — so observers of the new gen see both
235	                // arrived==0 and reset_counter==0.
236	                atomicExch(g_arrived, 0u);
237	                atomicExch(reinterpret_cast<unsigned*>(reset_counter), 0u);
238	                __threadfence();
239	                atomicAdd(g_generation, 1u);
240	            } else {
241	                unsigned backoff = 32u;
242	                while (*reinterpret_cast<volatile unsigned*>(g_generation)
243	                       == my_gen) {
244	#if defined(__CUDA_ARCH__) && (__CUDA_ARCH__ >= 700)
245	                    __nanosleep(backoff);
246	                    backoff = (backoff < 1024u) ? (backoff << 1) : 1024u;
247	#endif
248	                }
249	            }
250	            __threadfence();   // §1.14 ACQUIRE.
251	        }
252	
253	        __syncthreads();
254	    }
255	};

259	//  needs. The host allocates these (all zero-initialized) and passes their
260	//  device pointers to the kernel. Grouping them keeps the generated kernel
261	//  signatures uniform across all 99 cells.

265	    unsigned* g_arrived;       // §1.4 GridBarrier arrival count

267	    int       n_tasks;         // parameter tensors this step

## 1. `wgmma.cuh` — the hand-rolled ss-WGMMA (HGMMA) substrate

Namespace `sg::sm90::wgs` (it **REOPENS** the same namespace as `warp_specialize.cuh`, does not fork — `wgmma.cuh:36-38`). Includes ONLY `<cuda_bf16.h>`, `<cuda_runtime.h>`, `<cstdint>` — self-contained, no CUTLASS dependency (`wgmma.cuh:122-124`). All PTX guarded on `__CUDA_ARCH__ >= 900`; pre-sm_90 compiles to a documented scalar/no-op fallback so the codegen matrix still builds.

### 1.1 Instruction implemented
`wgmma.mma_async.sync.aligned.m64nNk16.f32.bf16.bf16` — the asynchronous warp-group MMA, **shared-shared ("ss") variant**: BOTH A and B operands live in shared memory and are addressed via 64-bit smem matrix descriptors (`wgmma.cuh:6-11`, PTX ISA §<ip>.1). Accumulator is fp32 in registers. M is fixed at 64 (the atom); K is 16 (`kWgmmaAtomM=64`, `kWgmmaAtomK=16`, `wgmma.cuh:142-143`).

### 1.2 Tunable defaults (THIS file's perf levers)
- `SG_TUNED_TILE_N` default **128** (output tile width; {64,128,256}) — `wgmma.cuh:133-135`
- `SG_TUNED_TILE_M` default **128** (token-tile rows/CTA; issued as TILE_M/64 stacked m64 atoms) — `wgmma.cuh:136-138`
All `#ifndef`-guarded so an untuned/lifted build composes a correct kernel; the kernel-autotuner injects `-DSG_TUNED_*` per-TU (`wgmma.cuh:128-138`).

### 1.3 Swizzle modes (`SwizzleMode` enum, `wgmma.cuh:167-172`)
Encoding = CUTLASS `cute` LayoutType: **NONE/INTERLEAVE=0, SWIZZLE_128B=1, SWIZZLE_64B=2, SWIZZLE_32B=3** (NOT size-ascending). `wgmma.cuh:152-155` flags that an earlier draft had 32B/128B swapped.
**CORRECTNESS-PATH NOTE (`wgmma.cuh:157-165`): the gated/tested numerics path ships `kSwizzleNone`.** 128B-swizzle is a perf-phase optimization (bank-conflict elimination) exposed as a template param but NOT required for any correctness gate.

### 1.4 Smem matrix descriptor (`SmemDesc{uint64_t desc;}`, PTX ISA §<ip>.4)
- `smem_desc_encode_addr()` (`wgmma.cuh:181-189`): `(__cvta_generic_to_shared(ptr) & 0x3FFFF) >> 4`. Low 4 bits MUST be 0 → operand tiles MUST be 16-byte aligned (silently drops bits otherwise).
- `make_smem_desc<Swizzle>(base, lbo_bytes, sbo_bytes, base_offset)` (`wgmma.cuh:219-241`): packs bits: addr[13:0], LBO>>4 @[29:16], SBO>>4 @[45:32], base_offset @[51:49], swizzle @[63:62].
- **Canonical Major-K builders** `make_desc_A_kmajor<MN,Swizzle>` / `make_desc_B_kmajor<MN,Swizzle>` (`wgmma.cuh:274-288`): for both, **LBO = MN*16 bytes, SBO = 128 bytes**. Derived from `cute::make_gmma_desc<Major::K>` / `Layout_K_INTER_Atom`.
- **Required smem layout** (`wgmma.cuh:243-269`): NOT a plain row-major block. The CUTLASS-canonical Major-K INTERLEAVE layout: element (mn,k) at bf16 index `idx(mn,k) = (k/8)*(MN*8) + mn*8 + (k%8)` — K=16 is two stacked 8-wide core matrices, each an MN×8 row-major block of 128-bit rows.

### 1.5 fp32 accumulator fragment (`WgmmaAccum<N>`, `wgmma.cuh:314-324`)
- `static_assert(N % 8 == 0)`; holds `kRegs = N/2` fp32 regs per thread; `.zero()` clears all. 128 warpgroup threads together hold the 64×N tile.
- **Authoritative fragment decode** `wgmma_frag_decode(tid_in_wg, i, N, &row, &col)` (`wgmma.cuh:343-364`): the SINGLE source of truth for thread→(row,col) used by BOTH the epilogue store AND the gate's reference comparison. Decode (PTX ISA §<ip>.3 .f32 accumulators):
  - `warp = tid>>5`, `lane = tid&31`; `slab = i>>2`, `within = i&3`; `row_half = within>>1`, `col_par = within&1`
  - `row = 16*warp + (lane>>2) + 8*row_half`
  - `col = (lane&3)*2 + col_par + 8*slab`

### 1.6 Choreography helpers (all inline PTX, all `.sync.aligned`)
- `wgmma_fence()` → `wgmma.fence.sync.aligned` (§<ip>.2) — `wgmma.cuh:374-378`
- `wgmma_commit_group()` → `wgmma.commit_group.sync.aligned` (§<ip>.5) — `wgmma.cuh:385-389`
- `wgmma_wait_group<N>()` → `wgmma.wait_group.sync.aligned %0` with `"n"(N)` immediate (§<ip>.6) — `wgmma.cuh:398-403`. `<0>` drains all; epilogue MUST `wait_group<0>` before reading accumulators.

### 1.7 The per-shape issue overloads (`wgmma.cuh:439-563`, guarded `__CUDA_ARCH__>=900`)
Explicit overloads, each listing exactly N/2 `"+f"` accumulator registers, descriptors as `"l"` u64 inputs, immediate tail `..., 1, 1, %transA, %transB` (scaleA=scaleB=1 hard-fixed — no operand negation):
- `wgmma_issue_n8` (4 regs), `_n16` (8), `_n32` (16), `_n64` (32), `_n96` (48), `_n128` (64).
- N={8,16,32} are the self-test "ladder"; N=64 is the DESIGN ragged-edge tile; N=96 is the decoder head (V=99); N=128 is the DESIGN default.
- Dispatcher `wgmma_m64nNk16_bf16<N,ScaleD,TransA,TransB>` (`wgmma.cuh:573-591`): `static_assert(N in {8,16,32,64,96,128})`, `if constexpr` selects the overload. ScaleD=0 OVERWRITES (D=A·B), ScaleD=1 ACCUMULATES (D+=A·B).

### 1.8 K-chain mainloop helper (`wgmma_mainloop_kchain`, `wgmma.cuh:617-644`)
Template `<N, TransA, TransB, bool FenceBeforeFirst=true, DescGen>`. The whole choreography in one call:
- optional `wgmma_fence()` (if FenceBeforeFirst)
- k=0: `gen(0)` → issue with **ScaleD=0** (overwrite, no pre-zero needed for fresh tile)
- `#pragma unroll 1` loop k=1..k_steps-1: `gen(k)` → ScaleD=1 (accumulate)
- `wgmma_commit_group()` then `wgmma_wait_group<0>()`
- **Determinism rule (DESIGN §3.1):** fixed ASCENDING k-order, one CTA owns the tile end-to-end, no work-steal split, no float atomics → bitwise reproducible. `gen` is a callback so the SAME mainloop serves the unpipelined gate (fixed pre-staged array) and the pipelined gate (ring-buffer stage) with bit-identical numerics (gate (c)).

## 2. `tile_pipeline.cuh` — the cp.async ring (producer/consumer double/triple-buffer)

Namespace `sg::sm90::wgs`; `prim = sg::sm90::primitives`. COMPOSES (no duplication) the substrate primitives: `Mbarrier`/`fence_async_proxy`/`warpgroup_reg_*`/`elect_one_sync` (warp_specialize), `cp_async_cg_16`/`commit`/`wait_group` (primitives), and the ss-wgmma engine (wgmma.cuh). Includes all three headers (`tile_pipeline.cuh:74-76`).

### 2.1 CONFIRMED: cp.async ring, NOT TMA
`tile_pipeline.cuh:199-204`: *"this uses cp.async (.cg.16), NOT TMA — DESIGN §4.1 item 3 makes TMA explicitly phase-2; phase-1 staging is cp.async."* The producer issues `prim::cp_async_cg_16` 16-byte copies, then `cp_async_commit()` + `cp_async_wait_group<0>()`, and uses the mbarrier purely as the cross-warpgroup ready signal (NOT byte-counting — it does NOT use the `cp.async.mbarrier.arrive` variant).

### 2.2 Tunable defaults (THIS file's perf levers, `tile_pipeline.cuh:86-97`)
- `SG_TUNED_PIPE_DEPTH` default **2** (double-buffer; {2,3,4} smem-capped) → bound to `Depth`
- `SG_TUNED_WG_COUNT` default **2** (1 producer + 1 consumer; fixed at 2 for phase-1)
- `SG_TUNED_PROD_REGS` default **40** / `SG_TUNED_CONS_REGS` default **232** — `setmaxnreg` targets (sum within 256-reg budget at 256 thr/CTA). **0 disables the rebalance** (portability/debug).

### 2.3 `TileGeom<N>` (`tile_pipeline.cuh:104-115`)
A tile = 64×16 bf16 = 2048 B; B tile = N×16 bf16 = N*32 B. `kStageBytes = kABytes + kBBytes`. Row strides 32 B. `kStageTxBytes = kStageBytes` (mbarrier expect-tx).

### 2.4 `TilePipeline<N,Depth>` (`tile_pipeline.cuh:142-189`)
Ring of Depth (A|B) stages + 2*Depth mbarrier words (full[Depth] then empty[Depth]).
- `full(s)` / `empty(s)`: construct an `Mbarrier` on-demand over `bars + s` / `bars + Depth + s` (Mbarrier has only an explicit ctor, no default ctor — so only the base pointer is stored).
- `stageA(s)` / `stageB(s)`: pointers into the ring.
- `smem_bytes()`: `Depth*kStageBytes + 2*Depth*8`.
- **`init_barriers()` (`tile_pipeline.cuh:180-188`): thread 0 inits each `full`/`empty` to count = 128 (a FULL WARPGROUP of arrivals).** Critical correctness note (`tile_pipeline.cuh:172-179`): an earlier draft used `init(1)` + per-warp `elect_one_sync` arrive, but `elect.sync` elects one leader PER WARP → 4 warps = 4 arrivals on a count-1 barrier → phase flipped an even number of times → **DEADLOCK** of the consumer's `try_wait.parity`. Fix: count=128 + all-128-threads-arrive.

### 2.5 `pipeline_produce_ktile` (`tile_pipeline.cuh:206-259`)
WG0 staging of one K-tile. `wtid = threadIdx.x & 127`. Scatters 16B (8 bf16) `cp_async_cg_16` copies from global row-major into the canonical Major-K layout: A is MN=64 (128 vectors), B is MN=N (N*2 vectors). A global row (mn,0..15) splits into two 16B halves: half0 (k0..7) → mn*8, half1 (k8..15) → MN*8+mn*8. Then `cp_async_commit()` → `cp_async_wait_group<0>()` → `fence_async_proxy()` (exactly ONE async-proxy fence per hand-off) → `pipe.full(slot).arrive()` (all 128 threads arrive).

### 2.6 `tc_pipelined_gemm_m64nNk16<N,Depth>` (`tile_pipeline.cuh:271-364`) — the turnkey GEMM
blockDim.x=256. WG0 (tid 0..127) = producer, WG1 (tid 128..255) = consumer.
- 16B-aligns the dynamic smem arena, constructs `TilePipeline`, `init_barriers()`, `__syncthreads()`.
- **Register rebalance** (gated on both `SG_TUNED_*_REGS != 0`, `tile_pipeline.cuh:291-294`): producer `warpgroup_reg_dealloc<PROD_REGS>()`, consumer `warpgroup_reg_alloc<CONS_REGS>()`.
- Producer loop: per k, `slot = k % Depth`; for k≥Depth `pipe.empty(slot).wait(empty_parity[slot])` then flip parity before overwriting; `pipeline_produce_ktile`.
- Consumer loop: `WgmmaAccum<N> acc`; `wgmma_fence()` once; per k waits `full(slot)`, builds `make_desc_A_kmajor<64,kSwizzleNone>` / `make_desc_B_kmajor<N,kSwizzleNone>` (both Major-K → **TransA=0, TransB=0**, cute Major::K==0); k==0 ScaleD=0 else ScaleD=1; `wgmma_commit_group()` + `wgmma_wait_group<0>()` per issue (so producer can't overwrite operands the async wgmma still reads); then `pipe.empty(slot).arrive()`. Epilogue: `tid_in_wg = threadIdx.x - 128`, decode via `wgmma_frag_decode`, store `gD[row*N+col]`.
- **Bit-identical to unpipelined kchain** (gate c): same ss-wgmma sequence, same ascending-k order; pipeline only changes WHEN each operand becomes available.

**NOTE on TransA/TransB discrepancy (correctness deviation to flag):** `wgmma.cuh:418-421` (API doc) says canonical is "TransA=0, TransB=1". But the ACTUAL pipeline call (`tile_pipeline.cuh:335-339`) and the self-test (`wgmma_selftest.cu:110-111`) both pass **TransA=0, TransB=0** with the comment "Both operands Major-K ⇒ TransA=0, TransB=0 (cute Major::K == 0)". The TransB=0 form (both Major-K) is the one actually exercised and gated.

Namespace `sg::sm90::mma`. **Gated behind `-DWITH_CUTLASS`; without it `#error` (`mma.cuh:875`)** — there is NO scalar fallback in this file; the project supplies cuBLAS fallback elsewhere. Includes `cutlass/...`, `cute/tensor.hpp`, `GemmUniversalAdapter`, `CollectiveBuilder`.

### 4.1 TMA is INSIDE CUTLASS, never hand-written here
`mma.cuh:34-44, 83-153`: CUTLASS 3.6 builds Hopper TMA tensor-map descriptors *inside* `op.initialize(args,ws,stream)` → `to_underlying_arguments` → `make_tma_copy_A/B_sm90` → `cuTensorMapEncode` (one per A and B + the epilogue C map), baked into `params_`. The old `device::Gemm` with no arch tag silently defaulted to SIMT/Sm70 (no tensor cores) — the fix is `GemmUniversalAdapter<GemmUniversal<...>>` from `CollectiveBuilder<arch::Sm90, OpClassTensorOp, ...>` which guarantees the Hopper WGMMA+TMA path.
**ELECT/MBARRIER BOUNDARY (honest note, `mma.cuh:145-153`):** the §3.4 elect/Mbarrier primitives compose a HAND-WRITTEN producer/consumer TMA staging loop, but the CUTLASS GEMM OWNS its TMA mainloop — there is no hand-written TMA staging in mma.cuh. Pairing elect/mbarrier with TMA belongs to the Stage-6 megakernel's hand-written path, NOT here. (Note: the Stage-6 hand-written path actually uses **cp.async**, per §2 — the only real hand-written TMA staging does not exist in the read files.)

- `GemmCacheKey{M,N,K, A,B,C}` — pointers part of key because a TMA tensor map encodes the global base address (address-stability invariant: a moved buffer → key change → MISS → rebuild, so a stale TMA descriptor is never launched against a relocated buffer, `mma.cuh:105-117`).
- `Sm90GemmCache<Gemm>`: 16-slot direct-mapped, **thread_local** (one per template instantiation per host thread — no mutex, single-thread-per-stream launcher). FNV-1a hash. Each entry OWNS its workspace (freed on eviction).
- `sm90_run_gemm_cached` / `_cached_out`: HIT → `e.op.run(stream)` (reuses baked descriptors); MISS → `make_cute_packed_stride` + Arguments + `can_implement` + `get_workspace_size` + `initialize` + `run` + install.

### 4.3 GEMM flavors (all 128x128x64 tile, 1x1x1 cluster, FP32 accumulate, KernelScheduleAuto)
- `Sm90Gemm<ElementInput>` (`:370`): RowMajor A·B, FP32 out. `gemm_fp16`/`gemm_bf16` (`:745`,`:756`).
- `Sm90GemmBT<ElementInput, LayoutBT>` (`:486`): B layout templated — RowMajor=C=A·B, ColumnMajor=C=A·Bᵀ. `sm90_run_gemm_bt`.

## 5. `megakernel_common.cuh` — Stage-6 L3 persistent megakernel coordination substrate

Namespace `sg::fused`. The uniform scheduler + barrier substrate every generated L3 megakernel composes (decoder/vit/mamba/SG2). Includes `warp_specialize.cuh`. Degrades to correct fallback on older arches.

- **`SG_TUNED_MEGA_BLOCK` default 256** (`:50-52`) = two 128-thread warp-groups. NEEDS-PARITY before shipping a non-default: must stay a multiple of warp-group size and re-validated on H100 (producer/consumer warp-spec assumes 256-thread shape).
- **§1.3 `sm_id()`** (`:65-73`): `mov.u32 %0, %%smid` — host launches gridDim.x == #SMs (one persistent CTA/SM) and indexes that SM's optimizer-state slice to keep it L2-warm.
- **§1.1/§1.2 `TaskQueue`** (`:91-117`): single global atomic counter `g_next_task` (host-zeroed). `next()` = `atomicAdd(g_next_task,1)` — the atomic IS the work-steal (no static partition; a CTA that drains early grabs the next index). `next_block(smem_slot)`: leader does the atomicAdd, broadcasts via shared, double `__syncthreads`.
- **§1.4 `GridBarrier`** (`:147-255`) — hand-built, reusable, **sense-reversing**, needs NO cooperative launch (scales past the cooperative-grid CTA cap):
  - State: `g_arrived` (count), `g_generation` (sense). Only thread 0 of each CTA participates; rest gated by `__syncthreads`.
  - **`sync()`** (`:157-210`): `__syncthreads` → leader samples `my_gen` (volatile read) → `__threadfence()` (§1.14 RELEASE) → `prev = atomicAdd(g_arrived,1)`. **Last arriver** (`prev+1==n_ctas`): `atomicExch(g_arrived,0)` → `__threadfence()` → `atomicAdd(g_generation,1)`. **Not last:** spin on volatile `g_generation == my_gen` with **exponential `__nanosleep` backoff** (start 32, cap 1024, sm_70+). Then `__threadfence()` (§1.14 ACQUIRE) → `__syncthreads`. Exactly TWO fences per CTA per barrier (minimum for correct release/acquire).
  - **`sync_reset(int* reset_counter)`** (`:222-254`): identical but the last arriver ALSO `atomicExch(reset_counter,0)` BEFORE the generation bump. Folds the task-counter reset into the barrier's last-arriver critical section → removes 2 standalone resets + 2 barriers (4→2 grid barriers per L3 step). Pass `ctx.g_next_task` as `reset_counter`.
- **§1.13/§1.14 fences:** acquire/release placed EXPLICITLY and MINIMALLY; no loose fences (correctness AND >10% perf footgun).
- **`PersistentContext`** (`:263-276`): `g_next_task, g_arrived, g_generation, n_tasks, n_ctas` + `queue()` / `barrier()` factory methods. Host allocates all (zero-init). "across all 99 cells" uniform signature.
